messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 CPU-backed latency breach on canary pool 'canary-gpu-east-2' detected (metric: inference.latency.p99). Threshold (2s) crossed at 2026-03-15T20:42Z. Paging on-call.

sara: saw this on the dashboard — p95 up too but p99 blowout. streaming stalls showing in traces.

cheng: is this the v6-rollout we put behind the canary? I pushed the traffic shadowing yesterday.

ryan: yep v6.0-quant-hotstart. Canary was 5% traffic for 00:30. started ~20:30Z.

michelle: logs show request queues piling on a subset of hosts, KV hits drop, lots of token re-computations.

emma: adding link to trace: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/trace/abc123 - you can see long stall spans during token fetch.

cheng: can someone run `redwoodctl canary status --pool canary-gpu-east-2` and `kubectl get pods -l canary=canary-gpu-east-2 -o wide`?

ryan: running now.

ryan: ```
$ redwoodctl canary status --pool canary-gpu-east-2
status: degraded
traffic_alloc: 5%
error_rate: 0.3%
latency_p95: 1.1s
latency_p99: 3.8s
replicas_healthy: 7/10
```

michelle: `kubectl` shows 3 pods with RestartCount > 5 and one with OOMKilled.

emma: customers hitting higher tail: acme-corp (prod), beta-integrations (staging) — ingest pipeline shows retries.

incident-bot: Customer impact tag: potential SLO degradation for customers on canary model routing. Notifying account-ops.

cheng: immediate mitigation options: 1) drop canary to 0% 2) route new requests to fallback model (v5-stable) 3) roll back canary build. Which first?

sara: prioritize customer availability — do fallback routing first, then drop allocation. rollback if fallback doesn't help.

michelle: I'll enable fallback policy. `redwoodctl route set --pool canary-gpu-east-2 --fallback v5-stable`

deploy-bot: Command accepted. Applying routing change...

deploy-bot: Routing update complete. New requests for canary group now prefer v5-stable; existing in-flight still to v6 where possible.

ryan: metrics update: p99 dropped from 3.8s -> 2.1s in last 60s but still above SLO. p95 back to 900ms. traces show fewer streaming stalls but some hosts still degraded.

emma: confirm: any customer-facing errors? SLO error budget burn near 12% for acme-corp. No widespread 5xx increase.

cheng: ok next: drain the 3 misbehaving pods and cordon hosts to stop new allocations. `kubectl drain podX --ignore-daemonsets --force`

michelle: doing drains now, will also bump canary down to 1% to reduce surface area.

michelle: canary traffic set to 1% (was 5%).

ryan: p99 stabilized ~1.9s. Still above target but trending down. Host-level disk latency on two nodes spiked — I see increased io wait (iowait ~32%).

emma: ops note: hotspot seems correlated with the new kv-eviction policy in v6 which increases synchronous disk reads under certain sequence lengths.

cheng: given this, I'm recommending rollback of v6 on the canary pool and a full investigation of kv eviction path. Rollback to v5-stable for canary nodes.

sara: +1. We need to avoid further SLO burn. Who will execute rollback?

michelle: I can trigger canary rollback. Running `redwoodctl rollout rollback --canary canary-gpu-east-2 --to v5-stable`

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated. Canary traffic routing will be reverted over 2 minutes.

deploy-bot: Rollback complete. Model version v5-stable reinstated on canary pool.

ryan: post-rollback metrics: p99 now 650ms, p95 180ms. KV hit-rate rising back to baseline. No new OOMs.

emma: sending a brief to account-ops and customer-support about potential impact window 20:30Z-20:50Z. acme-corp saw elevated tail latencies; recommend proactive note.

cheng: great. On-call handoff: sara, you're staying on it for 30 minutes to watch for regression, then hand off to next oncall if stable. Add action item for postmortem: reproduce kv eviction behavior with v6 on canary infra, check quantization path.

sara: taking it. will watch for 30m and then update timeline. adding Slack thread to incidents-playbook channel for postmortem notes.

michelle: saved relevant logs and exported traces: `gs://redwood-logs/incident-2790001111/`

incident-bot: Incident resolved: p99 back under threshold. Please file postmortem if follow-up required.

emma: I'll coordinate the postmortem with product/rls/infra. tagging @cheng to lead technical writeup.

cheng: will do. preliminary RCA: v6 kv-eviction path interacts poorly with node storage under bursty streaming sequences — causes sync reads and CPU stalls. Also a misconfigured memory limit on canary pods triggered OOMs. Fix plan: revert unsafe kv change in v6, add unit tests for streaming sequence edge-cases, adjust pod memory request/limits.

sara: logging final handoff — monitoring for 30m. If nothing odd, I'll close and ping ops. :white_check_mark:

michelle: thumbs up. I'll schedule rollback verification test run in staging tomorrow morning.

emma: thanks all. brief to legal/accountops drafted and sent. We'll follow up in postmortem.
